message: All right, here is the new $300 contract, with milestones organized by scene. I uploaded a revised script to the shared google folder; it contains only a few minor changes from the previous version. You can skip the text cards because I can handle those myself, so there may be some money left over for fine-tuning, but we’ll see how things progress. Please let me know if anything is unclear. Thanks!
Understood. I will review the script again and write to you if any questions come up.
Ok great
Ppl
Please make every effort to maintain the correct style as well. The style seems capable of gradually drifting or changing, and it is very important to me that the artistic style be perfect.
Yes. I will begin by generating an image and then send it to you to approve.
I am currently reviewing the images from the CC1 storyboards. Should the video imagery be in color, or should it be black and white?
I also have a question about the video’s format: should it be vertical or horizontal?
The final video should be entirely in color. Storyboards are frequently black and white as a cost-saving measure.
Vertical 9:16 aspect ratio
Hello! I am about to send you a link to the key images for the first scene’s video. I created them based on your images, so please look them over and leave comments.
Here is the link: [URL_001]
If possible, when a frame works, please post its name here followed by "+". If something needs to be revised, post the frame’s name along with your comment about it.
Sent notes via email

For shots taken from such a distant angle, the image resolution cannot be improved further; it depends on the shot angle. Did you zoom in on the hero? Also, in some frames where the pulse is moving, there is no need to use many images, as this is specified in the video.
I will make another attempt at changing every image.
However, I would also like to show you a version of the video fragment that we could produce without detailed photo frames, using only photographs of the characters and the location.
I wanted to ask something else as well. Your video includes an aerial shot during 0-5 seconds, but that shot does not appear in the script. Do you want shots like that added?
Regarding the quality of the sets, these are the images you provided, and this is the greatest improvement possible.

Does that mean low-angle shots automatically have low resolution, while shots from higher angles can achieve better resolution? I’m willing to change the shot angles if that will improve the quality of the set images. I wasn’t aware of that limitation.
I do want the opening aerial establishing shot, but it is a lower priority. We can hold off on it until we have confirmed that everything else we need is completed before using time on that shot.

Would it be worthwhile to generate new set images as the starting frames so that the sets are higher quality? I’m fine with doing that if it would be beneficial. I didn’t realize we would be limited to the resolution of my set images, and I don’t believe their quality is high enough.
Yes, the hero is shown here from a distant perspective. His details cannot be seen, although he is marked.
I was asking for clarification because this will matter later if you decide to add your voiceover. It is preferable to account for that immediately when determining the timing of the shots.
Yes, it does have an effect. May I create similar backgrounds?
Should we replace the distant shots with medium and close-up angles?
If possible, I would like to retain the long, wide shots at the start of the sequence. I’m okay with creating new sets, provided they match the intended style and remain consistent from shot to shot.
The first set is wide, the second set is mid, and the third set is closer.
Ok

Sorry, my wording was probably confusing because I used "set" in different ways. There are three PAIRS of images, and every pair contains 1 shot of Q and 1 shot of Deadwax. The first two images are long/wide shots, the second two are mid shots, and the third pair consists of closer shots from the waist up.
Let’s review the specifics once more so that I do not complete the wrong work. Are we keeping the images like this, with the background included? I improved them slightly.
For CC1\_1, does this distant angle work for you? At this angle, the hero will generally not be in focus; we display the frame for a few seconds without zooming in.
For CC1\_3, is this the intended angle?
I have revised several of the shots. Before I can complete the remaining ones, we need to align on these, so please review them.
You can review them here: [URL_002]
I sent my notes on this group of images by email.
Thank you, I have read the notes. About the sets: they are actually different, although they are fairly similar. Isn’t that degree of similarity appropriate?
They may appear similar, but I only enhanced the images you supplied; the images are different.
Yes, they are considerably more similar than they were in my versions.
Please take a look here: [URL_001]
The new images are available here: [URL_002]
These look significantly better. I sent my notes by email. Thanks!
I updated the image based on your notes and included a few additional frames here: [URL_002]
Honestly, I do not understand what you dislike about the Q set, since I am only changing its scale and not altering anything else.
May I send the background and the character without the background as separate files, so that you can demonstrate how you would prefer it?
Scaling in Photoshop
The issue is that AI can’t produce a perfect crop while preserving the details you identified. Okay, I can handle it as you requested using only Photoshop, and I’ll send you the result later.
[URL_002] I cropped these in Photoshop without AI. If they still aren’t correct, then I no longer know how else to do it.

Ok, these are looking good. There are just a few minor issues left: I can now see the bridge behind Q around his waist, which is poorly placed. Could you remove that bridge as well as the one directly above his head? In the Q images, please keep only the upper bridge so the lower ones aren’t in the way. These images are also missing the character shadows—could you restore those without changing anything else? Thanks for continuing to work through this!
Could you explain in more detail what type of shadows you mean?
just shadows of characters?
Also, have you reviewed images 8a, 8b, 9a, 9b, and 9c?
Yeah, the characters had shadows in the earlier renders, but those shadows aren’t present in these renders.
Sorry, I’ll take a look at the other images.
I added updated CC1-CC6, along with new shots you haven’t commented on yet. Please review them, thanks. [URL_002]

Hello! If possible, I’d be very grateful if you could provide all requested revisions ahead of time. Receiving adjustments piece by piece often means having to redo everything from the start, which requires extra time. Thank you very much for understanding!
You said that the angle was changed in the СС8 script, but I’m supposed to follow your storyboard exactly, right? I’m confused by this.
Has everything related to СС9 changed too?

I wanted to clarify that when the script and storyboard differ, it may create extra work that wasn’t originally expected. To keep the process running smoothly, it would be very helpful for the script to match the storyboard from the outset, or for any revisions to be communicated in advance. Thank you!

You’re absolutely right, and I’m sorry. I should have highlighted those changes more clearly and revised the storyboard reel.

There aren’t any other major changes of that kind, but I’ll review the script and identify any additional minor tweaks so the direction is 100% clear.

Again, I apologize, and I’ll follow up with that information.
Do I need to revise СС2 and СС4? Also, for the scenes beginning with СС7, please let me know whether they match the storyboard.

Please pause for the moment. Before you continue working, I want to review everything and compile a list of any other changes so we don’t waste effort. I’m traveling today, so I won’t have it ready until tomorrow or the following day.
There are just a few minor adjustments, but I want to identify each one clearly.
Okay
If you’d like, you can continue with CC1 using the notes I gave you yesterday about the energy blast.
At this point, I don’t understand which frames are supposed to be included or how many there should be. I mean CC8 and CC9.
Ok, give me a day and I’ll document every change and provide detailed descriptions for the remaining shots in CC1.

Ok, one issue I’m running into is that I can’t create the angles I want for these shots. The desired angles were already specified in the script, and the script also noted that the storyboard angle was incorrect. However, if you were working only from the storyboard reel rather than the script, then we were misunderstanding each other. If I’m unable to create the angle I want, add it to the storyboard reel, and show it to you that way, what workflow would be effective for you? How should I communicate the desired angle so you can render the shot accurately?
I’m putting hours into trying to create images with the right angles, but I still can’t get them, so it’s consuming a huge amount of time and energy...

I understand. Even when I focus only on the script, I still can’t determine how many frames are required for CC1\_7 Mid-Shot, CC1\_8 3⁄4 Mid Shot, CC1\_9, and CC1\_11. Do none of the shots match your city board? What specifically was changed?

I can create the shots only according to how I interpret the written description, not necessarily how you picture them, so misunderstandings may occur. Could you perhaps give me a short explanation of the changes in your storyboard?
Please review the footage containing the previous revisions here: [URL_002]
What do you think of this option with 8 frames? Without a storyboard, it’s actually difficult to determine which frame you need.

Ok, I’ll identify anything that differs from the storyboard reel and provide very detailed descriptions of those shots. Before generating any frames, you can ask me questions or request clarification.

Another difficulty I’ve had is maintaining the character details I prefer within the style I want. If I provide two images—one showing the desired character details and another showing the intended style—could you try generating an image that combines both?

I could also update the storyboard reel myself, but I’m not very good at doing that yet, and it takes me too long. Instead, I’d like to try more detailed shot descriptions, possibly supplemented with example frames I find online.

Also, just to be clear: although I mentioned making a digital comic book with still frames, I’d like to attempt the animation first. I’ll fall back to the digital comic book with still frames only if the animation doesn’t give good results or proves too difficult or expensive.
Okay. What should I work on now?
Nothing at the moment. Give me a day—I’m preparing complete descriptions for the shots that differ from the storyboard, along with the new character reference.
And if you feel any of this justifies additional funding, we can talk about it.

I’d prefer to wait until the end before deciding whether to add more money. I’m hoping the remaining sequences will be easier and that we’ll establish a good process, allowing those sections to move quickly. If, by the end, the project has required more work overall than we originally planned, I’m happy to pay more. I want to ensure you feel good about the arrangement.
Okay, I’ll wait for your directions. Have you viewed the revised CC1-CC7 footage?

Regarding the cost of the image-creation stage, everything is okay so far. Video creation is the most costly part, so I can’t assess that yet because we haven’t animated anything or discussed the animation style.
Hello! I wanted to check in about continuing our work. I hope everything is going well.
Hi, sorry—I’ve just been occupied with other things. I’ll send the updated images this afternoon.

Ok. Before continuing, I’d like to refine the character style somewhat. It keeps shifting, and I’ve struggled to keep it consistent and precise. Deadwax and Nova are close to what I want, while Q is the furthest away—he looks too clean, simple, and polished. I’m aiming for a rougher graffiti aesthetic. Could you quickly try applying this style to all three characters and send me the results?
You can see that it’s rougher and darker, with more sketch-like energy and a stronger attitude.
Out of the three, this one is my favorite in terms of his features and level of detail, if you need a target reference.

Sorry, but this isn't the way it should be handled. You provided me with a script containing the characters and a storyboard. I devoted a lot of time to creating an image using your earlier images. I was waiting to receive the scene details, and then you chose to change everything???
I'm sorry. Because I wasn't satisfied with the characters' appearance, I offered you additional money, and you said that was fine. That is why I made the request and the offer.
I'm still willing to pay for the work to be redone.
Are you asking to change one hero? It looks to me like his style would be different from the others?
Okay. I’d like us to work on the project more productively so I can create the video for you. Could you tell me what I should do next?
Could you let me know how much additional funding you would need to make just one attempt at changing the style of all three characters, then recreate the frames in their current form?
Are you asking to have new heroes created? The cost is $15 per hero.
Ah, okay. I had hoped it would be easier than that since all the character details are already dialed in and we have a target style. I'll try doing it myself.
yes, okay
Hi! How are things with you? I wanted to find out when we’ll resume work on the video.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I hope everything is going well.

I wanted to follow up to see whether you’ve decided what you want to do with the heroes and if you still intend to move forward with the project.

I also wanted to give you advance notice that I’ll be going on vacation soon, so I’d like to coordinate everything beforehand.

Thank you!

Hi, and sorry about the delay. We’re in the middle of moving, which has taken up every waking moment, and our nanny had to leave because of family matters, so I’ve been handling toddler duty :-\)

I definitely want to move forward, and I have some new images, although none of them are final yet.

Could you tell me when your vacation starts and how long you’ll be gone?

I really do want to continue…

All right, I understand. I will wait to receive more information from you.

My vacation is from 29.05 to 7.06
Hello, [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I hope everything is going well. I wanted to check in about the video work?

Hi, thank you for following up. The main issue is that it doesn't seem possible to achieve the look I want without investing more, and I may not be able to reach the animation quality I want either. I’d be game if you could help refine the look a little and run a few more animation tests, but I can't justify using up our contract on further look development or additional animation testing when I’m not confident we can achieve the desired result.
How much time did you put into the still frames that we worked on in April?
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], to be honest, I can’t recall exactly how much time I spent working on the still frames in April.
Thank you for clarifying. I understand the situation. What would you like to do next?
